concepts.def: All the organisms living in a particular area (community) and the non-living (abiotic) components with which they interact.
The place where an organism lives, characterised by particular abiotic and biotic conditions.
An organism's role within an ecosystem, including how it obtains energy and interacts with biotic/abiotic factors.
Maximum population size that an environment can sustain indefinitely given available resources.
Directional change in a community over time; pioneer species colonise, leading to a climax community.
Number of individuals of a species in a given area, often estimated using quadrats or mark-recapture.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Ecology & the Environment — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Ecology & the Environment brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Ecology & the Environment.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
